questions.prompt: Booking edits might still be occurring, but the account-compromise hypothesis has low confidence. Which triage record follows the chapter's priority model?

options.text: Delay every decision until compromise is proved
Record possible harm, time sensitivity and confidence separately, with a review trigger
Label the account compromised because urgency is high
Mark the matter low priority because the detector may be wrong

questions.explanation: Potential harm and urgency can be high while the cause remains uncertain. The incident lead records a provisional priority and the condition that would change it, then seeks a bounded authorized check.

questions.prompt: An edit was within its named authorization, but an owner-approved later comparison finds the booking value wrong. What do the chapter's A and M propositions say?

options.text: A is true and M is true; authorization and state mismatch are separate findings
A is false because a bad value always proves unauthorized work
M is false because authorization guarantees a correct service outcome
Both propositions identify the human who performed the edit

questions.explanation: A concerns permission for the particular operation at its time. M concerns a mismatch against an approved target at comparison time. Neither alone supplies the causal link or human attribution.

questions.prompt: Two SHA-256 checks of a saved E1 copy match. Which conclusion is supported without adding evidence?

options.text: The source log contained every relevant event
The producer clock was accurate
The checked byte sequence was consistent between the two checks
The exporter had authority to collect all patron records

questions.explanation: A matching digest supports a limited byte-consistency claim for the checked copy. It does not establish source completeness, timestamp correctness, collection authority or event truth.

questions.prompt: In the optional T2 replay, the same event-time window is queried at 09:12 and 09:20. Why can L2 appear in the later result?

options.text: Its event happened after 09:12
The later query changed the account filter
Its 09:10 event was ingested at 09:18, after the first query
L2 was added to the canonical R-series case

questions.explanation: L2's event time lies inside the half-open window, but it was not visible in the queried store until 09:18. A quiet earlier query reports visibility at that run time, not that no event occurred.

questions.prompt: A custodian confirms a narrow source hold, and an analyst has a separately hashed export. What still needs separate verification?

options.text: Nothing: the two receipts prove complete event coverage
The hold's actual source and interval effect, and the copy's provenance and scope
Only whether the file name contains the case ID
Whether the analyst can copy every unrelated patron field

questions.explanation: A source-hold control and a collected copy are distinct objects. A receipt or digest cannot by itself show that all source records existed, that deletion stopped for the intended scope or that the export was complete.
questions.source: Chapter 2, Lesson 08, §2.8a, source-hold and copy lifecycles

questions.prompt: R15 mentions a 24-hour retention duration for detailed booking-audit records. May P-B identity records use that same deadline?

options.text: Yes, all sources in one case share a retention clock
Yes, if the analyst has already requested an export
No; obtain the identity custodian's own availability and retention facts
No; identity records can never expire

questions.explanation: P-A and P-B concern different source paths. The identity-source retention period is not supplied, and R15 does not provide the booking source's policy anchor either. Preserve both uncertainties and contact the relevant custodians.

questions.prompt: R14 reports no further edit in its queried range. Which wording survives a possible late-arriving matching row?

options.text: No edit occurred anywhere after R9
No matching row was visible in this query as run, within its declared bounds
The account was inactive for the rest of the day
The logging pipeline was complete and delay-free

questions.explanation: A negative query is bounded by source, filter, event window, ingestion and run time. Without a completeness guarantee it cannot exclude delayed rows or events outside the envelope.

questions.prompt: An application event names desk-a beside a booking change. Which follow-up is justified before naming a human actor?

options.text: Treat the account label as the employee's identity proof
Join every available record and publish a patron list
Request bounded identity/session evidence and retain alternative explanations
Discard the booking event because it lacks device detail

questions.explanation: A shared or named account label does not establish which human used it. The chapter calls for a scoped, authorized discriminator and preservation of contradictions and missing fields.
questions.source: Chapter 2, Lesson 09, §2.9, correlation without actor invention

questions.prompt: An approved comparison finds two mismatches among five selected bookings. What is the defensible impact statement?

options.text: Exactly two patrons were harmed in the whole service
Two of five selected IDs mismatched their approved targets under the comparison rules
The other three bookings are automatically confirmed correct
Every ticket represents a distinct affected booking

questions.explanation: The numerator applies only to the defined selected frame. Ticket count, distinct booking count, confirmed mismatches and affected people are different measures; the unexamined population remains unmeasured.

questions.prompt: R9 records a 09:03 edit but was released to learners only in Round B. Can a 09:05 decision cite it as observed evidence?

options.text: Yes, because event time precedes the decision
Yes, if R9 supports the eventual conclusion
No; freeze the R1–R8 decision and add R9 in a later version
No; an edit record is never usable in any decision

questions.explanation: An event's timestamp is not its availability to the responder. The 09:05 checkpoint has R1–R8; R9 can inform the 09:20 revision without retroactively improving the earlier record.
